newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to step up police control on Chechen border.
newsitem.headline: Russia to step up police control on Chechen border.

text.p: Russia will beef up its police presence along the border with the breakaway region of Chechnya, Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov said on Monday.
"The reason for taking such measures are the most recent events on the border," Interfax news agency quoted Kulikov, a strong opponent of Chechen independence, as saying.

Kulikov said he was referring to an explosion last Friday on a railway track in Dagestan, which borders Chechnya, which killed five and wounded two rail workers, and to other threats issued by the Chechen rebels against Russians.

He said 300 to 350 cars a day entered Russia proper from Chechnya with food, fuel and weapons without proper checks, adding that President Boris Yeltsin had ordered the tightening of security along the border.
On Monday Chechnya went to the polls to elect a new president and parliament, in line with a peace accord that halted 21 months of fighting between rebel guerrillas and Russian troops last August.
All the main candidates for president support the region's full independence from Moscow.

But Moscow insists that the territory is still part of the Russian Federation, and a deputy foreign minister said on Sunday Moscow was ready to break off ties with any country that granted diplomatic recognition to Chechnya.
Last week Kulikov said Russia should be ready to send troops back into Chechnya if ethnic Russians still living in the mainly Moslem region came under attack.
